notes: The clean diagnostic UMD accepts the 64x48 BGRA8 shared target descriptor and calls AllocateCb, which fails with E_INVALIDARG. This corrects the v27 report inference that descriptor validation failed before AllocateCb.
Incremental MSBuild had reused an older UMD object after a header-only diagnostic edit in v27. The new standalone builder requires a clean build and records source/binary hashes.
The agent server restarted during this installation. The VM and storage tunnels continued running. The debugger and remote console were reattached.

The debugger recovery log was inadvertently reopened with an unsupported append option; earlier recovery entries were overwritten. The retained allocation trace starts after that reopen and records the debug4 attempt: Windows OpenAllocations succeeds and CreateVidMmAllocations returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER. Earlier debug-attempt stdout/stderr and exit records are preserved, but their earlier kernel traces are unavailable.
Debugger pauses affected elapsed times. These are functional diagnostics, not performance measurements.

Microsoft render-only sample documents that shared allocations can be CPU visible only when exclusively in an aperture segment. Our current shared allocation uses a memory segment with CpuVisible=1. This is the next correction to validate; this report does not claim the fix works.
